name: Hair gloss / glaze

lead: Hair gloss or glaze treatments are used to make hair look shinier and smoother.
Reference material describes how conditioners and colorants affect shine, but no clinical studies of gloss products were found.

paras: Treatments coat the hair or smooth the cuticle so light reflects more evenly. Laboratory work shows luster depends on hair structure and pigmentation [2].
Related color products may cause irritation or allergic reactions [1]; effects wash out over time.

lead: A hair gloss or glaze is a shine-boosting treatment used in salons and at home to make hair look glossier and smoother. Encyclopedia coverage of hair coloring does not describe glosses or glazes specifically, though it describes toners that adjust undertones and semi- and demi-permanent colorants that coat or sit beneath the cuticle [1].

Shine relates to how light scatters from the hair surface. Laboratory research has examined hair luster and how treatments change it, but no clinical studies of gloss or glaze products were found [2][3].

paras: Conditioners are described as improving shine by coating the fiber, filling cuticle defects and flattening cuticle scales; silicones in particular are noted for increasing shine [4]. Weathering, bleaching, dyeing and heat styling strip the cuticle's lipid film, leaving a rougher surface [4]. Physical studies show hair luster depends on the outer structure and pigmentation of the hair [2], and image analysis methods have been used to quantify how treatments change luster [3].

Semi-permanent colorants contain no developer or ammonia and last about 4 to 8 shampoos; demi-permanent colors fade over roughly 20 to 28 shampoos [1]. Toners slightly adjust undertones of bleached hair [1]. Safety concerns discussed for hair dyes include irritation and allergic reactions [1].
